text.p: LaserMaster Technologies Inc said Thursday it expects to report a loss of $0.16 to $0.18 a share for the third quarter ended March 30.
Analysts' expectations are for a loss of $0.16 a share.
LaserMaster said revenues will be about $19.5 million.
In the year-ago quarter, the company posted a loss of $0.18 a share on revenues of $23.3 million.
The company cited delays in the start of one new original equipment manufacturer relationship and one nationwide U.S. distribution agreement for DesignWinder, it high-resolution eight-color printer.
Internal production plans and sales forecasts proved to be too optimistic regarding DesignWinder sales, the company said.
It said a pending OEM relationship is progressing with a multinational corporation that plans to begin production-level sales of a private-label DesignWinder during the June quarter.
Final quarterly results will be released April 22.

To address the changing environment and the working capital cash flow effects of the failure to deliver adequate sales in March, LaserMaster said it began implementing a worldwide workforce reduction of about 10 percent.
It said five senior executives have voluntarily agreed to substantial reductions in compensation until the company's financial picture improves.
LaserMaster also said it had implemented a special "inventory reduction strike force" intended to generate additional short-term cash by lowering inventory in the next two quarters.

It said previous inventory increases resulted from an early-stage manufacturing learning curve, a new production line for DesignWinder, and the scheduled buffer inventory as new media and ink formulations were added.
LaserMaster said it is seeking a corporate investor with sufficient resources to assist it in its quest to bring its next generation printing program through the feasibility phase.
Throughout the third quarter, LaserMaster said it was negotiating the sale of intellectual property related to its proprietary PressMate chemical-free imaging technology.

The contemplated business relationship had the potential to deliver a one-time multimillion-dollar benefit to quarterly net income, plus the potential for future royalties tied to manufacturing rights.
But late in March LaserMaster was informed that the suitor had decided to put a hold on the technology acquisition.
LaserMaster said the overall short-term impact of its quarterly revenue shortfall is that it will experience a depletion of working capital and negative cash flow for several months.
